startup.name: Pocket
startup.one_liner: Take Notes in the Real World
startup.description: Pocket makes a premium AI voice recorder, a hardware device plus software subscription that records and summarises conversations. It says it is growing fast in the US and Europe and has a team of 35 in San Francisco. Consumers and professionals pay for the device.

yc_acceptance.basis: Accepted to YC in this test, so this note is for completeness. From roughly 1 percent for a random applicant, the lifts are real sales of a shipping device, a large team of 35 and claimed fast growth. The cuts are a crowded AI recorder category with Plaud, a consumer hardware business, and no technical founder detail in the description.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because AI voice recorders are a crowded hardware category led by Plaud, hardware margins and returns are hard, and the pitch gives no number for sales, retention, return rates or subscription revenue to show that demand is real and lasting.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2018-2025 --calibration-only gave seed cond 79% (n=52), range 72 / 79 / 81%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Below the anchor because hardware needs larger capital and the category is crowded, but a team of 35 and claimed growth suggest it is past the pre-seed stage.

bands.rationale: Thin or small-check round, close to the standard YC deal plus a small angel or pre-seed extension, typical when traction is slow.
Core case: 2022+ seed medians in the researched cohort are about $3.2M raised, and 2026 public seed pre money medians are near $18M.
Upside: a hot-category seed led by a top seed fund after quick early revenue or usage.
Outlier large seed, seen in the hottest AI categories only and rare overall.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed above $500K fails to be recorded in the window if the company was already financed before the batch and its next round is a larger priced round later, or if investors view the category as won by Plaud, which reported over a million devices sold. Hardware inventory costs and returns could also make early investors hesitate, as with Penta Medical, which never raised after YC.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2018-2025 --calibration-only gave series_a cond 39% (n=41).
anchors.adjustment_reason: At the anchor; the team size and sales are a plus, hardware capital intensity a minus.

bands.rationale: Modest A or a down-leaning round after a slow year of growth.
Core case: 2022+ YC series A medians are about $15M raised, public series A pre money near $60M.
Upside A led by a large fund after strong, fast revenue growth.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails if unit sales stall once early adopters have bought, if the subscription attach rate is low and the business remains a hardware margin story, or if Plaud, Amazon's Bee or Meta ecosystem devices set price and feature expectations. Proxy shows hardware can reach Series B, but it still ended in a sale rather than a large independent company.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2018-2025 --calibration-only gave series_b cond 38% (n=16).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Slightly under the anchor because consumer hardware rounds are harder and phones may absorb the function.

bands.rationale: Smaller or flat B, often an extension for a company that is profitable but growing slower.
Core case: 2022+ YC series B medians are about $37M to $45M raised.
Upside B on fast growth in a large category, led by a major growth fund.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B fails if retention is poor, if customer acquisition cost rises as paid channels saturate, or if phone and earbud makers integrate always on recording into hardware people already carry. Large consumer hardware rounds require clear subscription revenue and positive unit economics, which few device companies show.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2018-2025 --calibration-only gave series_c cond 17% (n=6); stage_benchmarks.md full sample conditional 36%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Between the narrow consumer anchor and the full sample, since a category leader with hardware revenue could raise a large later round.

bands.rationale: Smaller late round or a growth extension, likely when growth has slowed but revenue is solid.
Core case: 2022+ YC series C medians are about $45M raised, public series C deal size near $77M.
Upside late round for a category leader with fast growth and strong retention.

ladder.why_it_fails: A later round fails if the product is overtaken by a platform device, if regulation or privacy backlash against always on recording restricts sales in Europe and some US states, or if growth plateaus below the scale late investors need to justify a large growth round for a device company.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The likeliest result is a stall as phones and larger device makers absorb voice capture, or a small acquisition by a bigger device company as happened to Bee and reportedly Limitless. A result above $1B would need Pocket to be a category leader with subscription revenue, which Plaud currently holds.

analogs.outcome_summary: Reached a Series B and was acquired, showing hardware startups can raise but exit small.

analogs.relevance: Note taking workspace for sales teams, Winter 2019.
analogs.outcome_summary: Shut down with no funding after YC, showing weak retention in note taking tools.
Shut down with no round after YC, a hardware failure.
Raised a seed and was acquired.

killers.risk: Plaud and big tech own the AI recorder category
killers.evidence: Plaud reported over a million devices sold and Amazon acquired Bee in 2025, so a late entrant faces price pressure and brand dominance.
killers.mitigation: Win on quality, speed and a premium design and lock in subscribers with a differentiated app.

killers.risk: Hardware economics and returns consume the capital
killers.evidence: Inventory, manufacturing minimums and returns are heavy cash costs for a young company, and consumer devices carry thin margins.
killers.mitigation: Raise early enough to fund inventory and track return rates and subscription attach.

killers.risk: Phones and wearables absorb recording and transcription
killers.evidence: Phone makers and earbud makers add AI note features, which could remove the need for a separate recorder.
killers.mitigation: Position as a professional tool with better capture and workflows than a phone.

competition_now.what: AI voice recorder devices and note app.
competition_now.traction: Reported over one million devices sold in 2025.

competition_now.name: Bee (Amazon) and Limitless
competition_now.what: Wearable AI note takers and memory devices.
competition_now.traction: Bee acquired by Amazon in 2025; Limitless status vendor reported only.

competition_now.name: Phone voice memo and meeting note apps
competition_now.what: Free built in recording and transcription.

technical_complexity.rationale: Transcription and summaries are commodity now, but a premium device needs hardware design, manufacturing supply chains and firmware, which are slow, capital heavy and hard for a small team to do well.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large device makers and the category leader can ship rival hardware or add the feature to existing devices within a year and have bigger distribution.

evidence.claim: Plaud reports over one million devices sold, showing paying demand for dedicated AI recorders.
Reviewers say the jury is still out on wearable AI success, so demand beyond early adopters is unproven.

roadmap.goal: Show repeat purchase and subscription retention, not just launch sales.
actions: Publish cohort retention and subscription attach numbers to investors.
roadmap.proof: Positive contribution margin per device and subscription attach above a stated target.

roadmap.goal: Raise a priced round above $500K to fund inventory and growth.
actions: Lock in a manufacturing partner with flexible minimums.
Grow Europe with local retail partners.
roadmap.proof: Rising monthly revenue and a lead investor in a priced round.

pros.point: Shipping product with a team of 35 and claimed fast growth.
pros.evidence: The description cites scaling in the US and Europe, with a large team for a new batch company.
Plaud reported over one million devices sold.

brand.name: Pocket
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Pocket" --era 2022+ gave kind real_word, 6 chars, 2 syllables.
strengths: Common word that suggests a small portable device
weaknesses: Shared with a well known read later app, hard to own in search
brand.rationale: A plain real word that conveys portability is a typical strong consumer name and helps word of mouth, but the name collision with an existing app limits search ownership; it is neutral overall.

narrative.headline: A real shipping consumer hardware company in a category led by Plaud, likely to raise a seed but with capital intensive later steps.
narrative.general_summary: Pocket sells a premium AI voice recorder with a subscription and says it is scaling quickly in the US and Europe with a team of 35. That is a large, shipping company at batch start, so a financing above the YC deal is likely. The risks are structural: Plaud leads the category with a reported million plus devices, Amazon bought Bee, and phone makers can add the same function. Hardware needs more cash and has thinner margins than software, so each later round is harder than for a typical software company. The likeliest path is one or two rounds and then a stall or acquisition by a larger device maker, with a smaller chance of category leadership.

assumptions: Forecast made blind from the batch start 2026-01-05 using only the input file and market searches.
Seed means a round above about $500K within about 12 months; Pocket may already have raised before the batch.
Consumer cohort n is small so anchors are only a guide.
Plaud sales figures are secondary reports.
